title_en: Lu Daolong v. Lu Kui et al. — copyright infringement dispute
ruling_gist_en: A work within the meaning of the Copyright Law refers to an intellectual achievement in the fields of literature, art, and science that possesses originality and is capable of being reproduced in a tangible form. Originality is a prerequisite and substantive requirement for defining a work within the meaning of the Copyright Law; it directly affects the legal protection of copyright in works and the assumption of liability for infringement. A genealogy primarily records the lineage of a surname clan or a branch thereof and the names and pedigrees of ancestors through the generations. With respect to information derived from source materials or the public domain, it lacks originality and should not be protected by copyright law.

full_text_en:
Lu Daolong v. Lu Kui et al. — copyright infringement dispute

Ruling Summary

A "work" within the meaning of the Copyright Law refers to an intellectual creation that is original and can be reproduced in a tangible form in the fields of literature, art, and science. Originality is a prerequisite and substantive requirement for defining a work within the meaning of the Copyright Law, as it directly affects the legal protection of copyright in the work and the assumption of liability for infringement. A genealogy primarily records the lineage of a surname family or a particular branch and the names and pedigrees of successive ancestors. Information derived from source materials or the public domain lacks originality and should not be protected by the Copyright Law.

Plaintiff: Lu Daolong, male, 58 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Sheyang County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendants: Lu Kui, male, 90 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Jian, male, 68 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Ticai, male, 60 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Sheyang County, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Weizhou, male, 70 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Jianhu County, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Yinghu, male, 64 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Sheyang County, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Lianhua, male, 62 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Sheyang County, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Weilang, male, 75 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Haiyang, male, 71 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Qi, male, 80 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Jianhu County, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Yingzhu, male, 51 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Lu Yingzhu (different character), male, 57 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Lu Daolong, filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants Lu Kui, Lu Jian, Lu Ticai, Lu Weizhou, Lu Yinghu, Lu Lianhua, Lu Weilang, Lu Haiyang, Lu Qi, Lu Yingzhu, and Lu Yingzhu (the second) in a dispute over copyright infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff is the copyright owner of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" and is legally entitled to the copyright of that work. The aforesaid work was created by the plaintiff on September 1, 1991, and first published in Jiangsu Province on September 2, 1991. Without the plaintiff's permission, the defendants, for profit, distorted, altered, and extensively plagiarized the contents of the plaintiff's copyrighted work, then compiled it into a book titled "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China" in 2009 and publicly published and distributed it. As of the date of filing the lawsuit, approximately 1,500 sets had been sold, and it was still on sale. The additional defendants Lu Ticai, Lu Weizhou, Lu Yinghu, Lu Lianhua, Lu Weilang, Lu Haiyang, Lu Qi, Lu Yingzhu, and Lu Yingzhu (the second) were the editors-in-chief and deputy editors-in-chief of Volumes 3, 4, and 5 of the first printed edition of the infringing publication, and deputy editors-in-chief of the second revised printed edition of "The Genealogy of the Lu Xiu Family of Yancheng" (Volumes 1 and 2). The defendants had already printed a third edition, which, although not publicly sold, had been donated to the Yancheng City Archives and the Lu Gong Memorial Temple. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order the defendants to immediately cease infringement, issue an apology to the plaintiff, and jointly and severally compensate for economic losses of RMB 760,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 100,000.

Defendants' Defense (Lu Kui and Lu Jian):
1. The vast majority of the content in "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" consists of genealogies of the Lu family created by Lu ancestors across generations. The plaintiff, Lu Daolong, does not hold any copyright over this genealogical content. "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" mainly comprises nine volumes of Lu family genealogies: one volume of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Yandu Hall, revised in the tenth year of the Yuanhe reign of the Tang Dynasty; six volumes of the "Lu Family Genealogy" revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign; one volume (Continuation 7) of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall, from the twenty-first year of the Republic of China; and one volume (Continuation 8) of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall, revised in 1989 by the plaintiff and his father Lu Ming. The plaintiff was born in 1965 and could not have participated in the compilation of these genealogies; he is not the author of these genealogies.
2. For personal gain, the plaintiff renamed the genealogies compiled by Lu ancestors as "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>," put his name on them, and appropriated them as his own. On August 29, 2012, the plaintiff, under the name of the "Yancheng Lu Family Genealogy Revision History Office," sent a letter of certification to the National Copyright Administration, falsely claiming to be the copyright owner of this literary work, thereby fraudulently obtaining a registration certificate.
3. Regarding the basis and source of the content of Volumes 4 and 5 of "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China," i.e., "The Genealogy of the Lu Xiu Family of Yancheng": This genealogy is mainly a comprehensive revision based on the Shidetang Yancheng "Lu Family Genealogy" compiled over a hundred years ago in the first year of the Xuantong reign of the Qing Dynasty (1909) by Lu Jiaju, a descendant of the seventy-fourth generation of Yuanhou Lu Tong (twentieth generation of Lu Xiu) and a tribute student of the Yuandao Gang. The use of the hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall" was determined by the editorial committee in accordance with records in "The Complete Works of Lu Zhonglie," the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the first year of Xuantong, and "Yancheng County Annals," among other books and genealogical documents, concerning the imperial decree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign of the Ming Dynasty (1619) that "pursuant to the memorial, the posthumous title 'Loyal and Martyr' be granted." This was done to remember and promote the patriotic spirit of the loyal and martyr ancestor who perished with the nation and to express respect for ancestors. Therefore, there is no infringement, and the plaintiff's claims should be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Court (Intermediate People's Court of Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province):

On October 8, 1984, Lu Ming (the plaintiff's father) and the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, donated to the Sheyang County Archives: six volumes of the "Lu Family Genealogy" revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign; one volume (Continuation 7) of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall from the twenty-first year of the Republic of China; one volume (Continuation 8) of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall revised in 1989; and one volume of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Yandu Hall revised in the tenth year of the Yuanhe reign of the Tang Dynasty — a total of nine volumes, referred to as the "old genealogies" by the plaintiff.

On September 1, 1991, the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, compiled "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" in 12 volumes. Volumes 1-6 were the "Lu Family Genealogy" revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign; Volume 7 was Continuation 7 of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall from the twenty-first year of the Republic of China; Volume 8 was Continuation 8 of the revised "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall; Volume 9 was the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Yandu Hall revised in the tenth year of the Yuanhe reign of the Tang Dynasty; the other three volumes were two volumes of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Yandu Hall and one volume of "Ancestral Scroll of the Lu Family of China." On January 28, 2013, Lu Daolong applied for registration with the National Copyright Administration and obtained copyright registration for "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>."

The defendants, Lu Kui and others, initiated the compilation of "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China" at the end of 2006. "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China" consists of five volumes: Volume 1 — "Study on the Origins of the Lu Family"; Volume 2 — "Biographies of Lu Figures" and "Lu Xiu, the Prime Minister for the Ages"; Volume 3 — "Unified Genealogy of the Lu Family"; Volumes 4 and 5 — "The Genealogy of the Lu Xiu Family of Yancheng." The first printing was in January 2009. The editorial board of "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China" comprised 167 members, with Lu Kui as the director of the editorial board, Lu Ticai as the editor-in-chief of Volumes 3, 4, and 5, and the other defendants as deputy editors-in-chief.

During the trial, the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, stated that Volumes 1-7 and Volume 9 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" were compiled by the plaintiff from the old genealogies between 1982 and 1984, and Volume 8 was created by the plaintiff himself. The content of Volumes 1-6 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" was unchanged from the six volumes of the "Lu Family Genealogy" revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign in the old genealogies; Volume 7 added content for one generation on pages 17-33, which was not present in the old genealogies. The plaintiff argued that the infringement by the defendants consisted of two parts. The first part was the defendants' plagiarism in Volumes 3, 4, and 5 of "The Complete Guide to the Lu Family of China" of the following content from Volumes 1 and 2 of his "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>": page 2 of Volume 1, "Preface to the Genealogy by the Eldest Son of the Song Chancellor"; page 5, "Preface to the Second Continuation of the Lu Family Genealogy"; page 7, "Preface to the Third Continuation of the Lu Family Genealogy"; page 15, "By Imperial Decree"; page 21, "Portrait of Lu Xiu"; page 22, "Portrait of Yao Gong"; page 23, nine portraits of successive Lu ancestors; page 32, "Portrait of Emperor Jingyan"; page 33, "Edict Praising Wen Tianxiang," "Postscript to the Correction of the Classic of Filial Piety"; page 34, "Letter Encouraging Chen Wenlong," "Record of the Danyang Pavilion"; page 35, "Poem at the Crane Forest Temple," "Poem in Praise of Gaozu Zhonglie Gong," "Poem in Praise of Zengzu Cunsan Gong," "Poem in Praise of Zu Huanyang Gong" to the end of the volume; page 12 of Volume 2, "Petition for Bestowing Posthumous Title on Chancellor Lu"; page 15, "Imperial Edict Granting Posthumous Title 'Loyal and Martyr'." The second part was the defendants' unauthorized use of the term "Loyal and Martyr Hall" from the plaintiff's Volumes 7 and 8 in the book "The Genealogy of the Lu Xiu Family of Yancheng," i.e., the use of the plaintiff's hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall."

A comparison was made between the contents of Volumes 1 and 2 of the involved "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" and Volumes 1 and 2 of the "Lu Family Genealogy" revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign (old genealogies). The comparison showed that the contents and order of Volumes 1 and 2 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" were identical to those of Volumes 1 and 2 of the old genealogies revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign. The content of the first part of the alleged infringement by the defendants, as claimed by the plaintiff Lu Daolong, was also present in Volumes 1 and 2 of the old genealogies revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign. The difference was that the old genealogies were in traditional Chinese characters, while Volumes 1 and 2 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" were in simplified Chinese characters. The hall name used on the covers of Volume 7 and Volume 8 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" and the old genealogy Volume 7 (revised in the jiashen year of the Guangxu reign) was "Loyal and Martyr Hall."

Opinion of the Court (Intermediate People's Court of Yancheng City):

The Regulations for the Implementation of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China provide that "work" within the meaning of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China refers to an intellectual creation that is original and can be reproduced in a tangible form in the fields of literature, art, and science. That is, the constituent elements of a work are originality and reproducibility. A work must be an independently completed result of the author. The plaintiff, Lu Daolong, submitted a "Copyright Registration Certificate" to prove his copyright in "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>." Because the Copyright Protection Center of China only conducts a formal examination of the application documents submitted by the plaintiff, the court must conduct a substantive examination of the source of the work, the creative process, and the originality of the work. Although the creation of a work may involve inheriting and drawing upon human cultural achievements and may cite the works of others during the creative process, the work must have distinctive features in the form of expression of its content.

1. Whether the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, holds copyright in the involved Volumes 1 and 2 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>." Upon examination, the involved Volumes 1 and 2 of the plaintiff's work do not contain independent conception or creative style; they are merely reproductions of the same text from the works of others. Therefore, Volumes 1 and 2 of the plaintiff's "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" do not constitute works within the meaning of the Copyright Law and are not protected by the Copyright Law.

2. Whether the hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall" used by the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, on the covers of Volumes 7 and 8 of "The Chronological Genealogy of the Lu Family of China <Lu Family Genealogy>" is original. A hall name, as a family's emblem or alias, used on a genealogy to indicate the surname and lineage, is a high-level summary of the characteristics of a particular surname family. The same surname may use the same one or several hall names. In this case, the hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall" is a typical example of a hall name based on a conferred title of nobility, posthumous title, or commendation. It originated from the allusion of the Ming Dynasty Wanli Emperor bestowing the posthumous title "Zhonglie Gong" (Loyal and Martyr Duke) on Lu Xiu, the Left Chancellor of the Southern Song Dynasty. The old genealogy, Continuation 7 of the "Lu Family Genealogy" of the Loyal and Martyr Hall from the twenty-first year of the Republic of China, also used the hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall." Therefore, the hall name "Loyal and Martyr Hall" was not original to the plaintiff.

Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 3 and Article 11 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 2 and 3 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on September 23, 2013:

Rejected the plaintiff Lu Daolong's claims.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither the plaintiff, Lu Daolong, nor the defendants, Lu Kui and others, filed an appeal within the statutory period. The judgment has become legally effective.
